annotations.title: Follow rule changes in a feed

description:
Can you tell me if the dog rules change at Carmel Beach before our trip? Can I follow changes near Lake Tahoe, or along I-5?
For hearing about changes later, without asking again: it answers with a feed link (Atom and JSON Feed) for one place, a town, county, area or neighborhood with a radius, or a highway's stops, which any feed reader can follow. It computes the links and counts only; it signs nobody up, stores nothing and sends no email.
Inputs: one of place (a place id from any answer, e.g. "carmel-beach"), near (a town, county, area, region or neighborhood, e.g. "Lake Tahoe", "Monterey", "Van Nuys") with radius_miles, or route (i-5, us-101, highway-1, i-15, i-80, us-50, or a Nevada route ending in -nevada) with from_mile and to_mile.
Returns atom_url and json_url, how many verification events, rule changes and corrections the scope had in the last 90 days, the page for the scope, and share_text: a sentence with the link, written for the traveler. An unknown name is an answer with did_you_mean.

Examples:
  - "Tell me if the rules change at Carmel Beach" -> place="carmel-beach"
  - "Can I get alerts for dog rule changes around Lake Tahoe?" -> near="Lake Tahoe"
  - "Follow changes on the Grapevine stretch of I-5" -> route="i-5", from_mile=170, to_mile=222

from_mile.description: With route: start of the stretch, in route miles

near.description: A city, county, area, region or neighborhood in California or Nevada, e.g. "Lake Tahoe", "Monterey", "Washoe County, NV", "Van Nuys"

place.description: One place by its id from any answer, e.g. "carmel-beach" (a close name is matched and labeled)

radius_miles.description: With near: miles around the town (an area or region is its own boundary; the radius is ignored)

response_format.description: 'markdown' for readable text, 'json' for structured data

to_mile.description: With route: end of the stretch, in route miles

name: dogpolicies_subscribe_changes

accepted.description: With bad_input: each argument that could not be read, with the values it accepts

atom_url.description: The Atom 1.0 feed for the scope

code.description: With an outcome other than ok: not_found, invalid, unavailable

did_you_mean.description: Close matches to what was asked for: towns, places, slugs or brands, best first

json_url.description: The JSON Feed 1.1 feed for the scope

last_90_days.description: Activity in the scope over the last 90 days: verification events (re-checks included), rule changes (events whose outcome is changed, plus the rule-change log) and correction tickets (the hosted server only)

nearest.description: When nothing is inside the radius: the nearest places in the data, with distance_miles

next.description: Calls that would answer the question, in words

outcome.description: Absent or ok: a normal answer. no_match: nothing in the data matches, see did_you_mean, nearest and next. bad_input: the arguments cannot be used as given, see next. partial: some of the ids were found, see missing. unavailable: a live source could not be read. None of these is an error.

page_url.description: The page for the scope (the place's record or the road-trip guide), when there is one

resolved_from.description: Set when a word was read as the value the tool uses: hotel as lodging, NB as north. Each key is the argument; asked is what was sent, used what it was read as

scope.description: What the feed follows: place, near or route, its id and label

share_text.description: A sentence with the feed link, written for the traveler

title: Follow rule changes in a feed
